newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche - No final decision yet on MGAM control.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche - No final decision yet on MGAM control.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Wednesday it had not yet reached a final decision on the extent to which it may place British unit Morgan Grenfell's unit trust business under stronger German control.

The bank also declined to comment on when Udo Behrenwaldt, a managing director of its German investment subsidiary DWS who was sent to London in September as an adviser to Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), would return to Frankfurt.

"Thoughts on the extent to which the bank will locate the control of its unit trust business more strongly at DWS have not yet been fully completed in all details," Deutsche spokesman Detlev Rahmsdorf said in response to a Reuter enquiry.
Deutsche had said in September that its decision to send Behrenwaldt to Morgan Grenfell was linked to a possible rerouting of management reporting lines for the unit trust business to Frankfurt.
That rerouting had been under consideration for several years but the issue came back to the fore due to the discovery of problems at three MGAM funds in September, the bank said.

Deutsche said at the time that Behrenwaldt had taken on a consultative role and would not take part in active management. DWS, or Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Wertpapiersparen mbH, is Deutsche's German fund management subsidiary.
Earlier on Wednesday, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell announced the departure of four key managers following a probe into irregularities at its unit trust business.
It named Robert Smith as the group's asset management head, replacing Keith Percy as chief executive of MGAM.

Their departures follow revelations of major problems in three MGAM funds last month. The discovery of misvaluations of speculative unlisted stocks led to to the temprorary suspension of the funds and a 180 million pound cash injection by Deutsche to shore them up.
